MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 3, 2020

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, June 3, 2020 in the Council Chambers
on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of Allegiance
by Commissioner Patrick, the meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECDD Director
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney's Office
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox stated that the previously noticed Special Planning
Commission Agenda has been postponed to a later date and will be
re-noticed. She also stated that staff had received news that
Planning Commissioner Terry L. Coleman is retiring from the Planning
Commission as of today.

Chairman Springs asked staff what was the Special Planning Agenda
item and was it related to what is being postponed to a later date?

Ms. Wilcox stated it had to do with a presentation to Planning
Commissioner Terry Coleman on his retirement, but that it is going
to be postponed to a later date.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None. This was confirmed by the AT&T Operator, no one requested to
speak.

Chairman Springs closed this segment, and opened the Planning
Commission Meeting Public Hearing.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-002 (SP-2020-003) 2631 WEST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD: A public hearing to consider an application
by Donare Davis, representing Urban Ink Gallery, for Special Use
Permit No. 2020-003 (SP-2020-003) to allow a tattoo parlor within
an existing 2,700 square-foot multi-tenant commercial building on
a 5,000 square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 2631
West Manchester Boulevard. (THIS ITEM HAS BEEN PULLED AND WILL BE
RENOTICED)

(6) NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2020-002 (DR-2020-002) 231 SOUTH LA BREA
AVENUE. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Andrew
Pociu, representing TRIBE SF, Inc., for Design Review No. 2020-002
(DR-2020-002) to allow exterior improvements to a 700 square-foot
tenant space within an existing three-story 16,350 square-foot
multi-tenant commercial building on an approximately 7,000
square-foot property at 231 South La Brea Avenue.

Ms. Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs Larry asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff several questions–
 About the elevation;
   Ms. Kay answered it is not a requirement.
 Will the canopy will be reviewed by public works, but not the
  planning commission?
   Ms. Kay stated that there will be a design review process with
  the planning division and an additional process from the public
  works department.
 He stated he would like to see what the canopy would look like?
   Ms. Kay stated the applicant did submit a rendering with their
  partial elevation that was submitted already.

Commissioner Trejo stated she had questions for staff –
 Although this is just a design review, in staff’s report, it
  mentions that the applicant will use the second and third floors
  for co-working spaces, what does this mean?
   Ms. Kay stated the concept the applicant is proposing, is for
  short term or long term office space rentals on the second and
  third floor in an open office area.
 So this is not just for the coffee shop correct?
   Ms. Kay stated that the coffee shop will be on the first floor
  and the applicant will be doing tenant improvements there where
  the design review is only for the facade improvements to the
  first floor coffee shop. The second and third floors will be
  for rentals.
 So does this mean the applicant does not have to come before the
  planning commission for any of the tenant improvements or use on
  the second and third floors?
   Ms. Kay stated no, that is a by-right use.
 Commissioner Trejo also asked about the signage for both the coffee
  shop and the co-working office space, will it be subject to signage
  review or site plan review?
   Ms. Kay stated that a mural is subject to a design review under
  the municipal code sign regulations, and any other type of
  signage typically goes through a sign adjustment or a sign
  permit, since it is a multi-tenant building it will also need
  a master sign program, but not to say it will have to come back
  to the planning commission, unless it goes through a sign
  adjustment and it is appealed.
 Has there been any work started on the project façade yet?
   Ms. Kay stated that there has been some tenant improvements
  along with the façade.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Since you mentioned the applicant will be renting out the second

  and third floors, will they be entering those floors from the first
  floor?
   Ms. Kay stated not through the coffee shop, and although it was
  not presented in the initial presentation this evening, mainly
  since it was not directly related to the coffee shop, but in
  the plans in the Planning Commission packet, there are plans
  from the rear of the building, for use of a stairwell that leads
  upstairs from the parking area.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff several questions-
 Is there also an entrance for the Coffee Shop on the first floor
  through the rear of the building? She stated she recently attended
  an event at this location, and the only way into the building at
  that time was from the rear, which meant the applicant was
  conducting business prior to coming to the planning commission.
   Ms. Kay stated yes, the applicant was operating in the building,
  and presently the applicant is under investigation by the Code
  Enforcement Division.
 Parking for this establishment, how will that be dealt with?
   Ms. Kay stated that the uses the applicant is proposing to
  conduct business are uses by-right and do not trigger any need
  for further parking requirements. Now should special events
  come up or gatherings then they would need to address parking
  at that time.
 Has the applicant mentioned any desire for sidewalk seating or
  anything like this?
   Ms. Kay stated that has not been proposed by the applicant. One
  point of clarification - the front opening for the coffee shop
  will be within the front/North area of the building.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 What about events being held upstairs on the second level?
   Ms. Kay stated that it is being investigated by Code
  Enforcement.
 So that type of action is not a by-right, or is it?
   Ms. Kay stated no, it is something that would need to go through
  a special use permit.
 If they propose in the future to do sidewalk dining, will the
  applicant need permits for that?
   Ms. Kay stated yes, because the applicant is in the downtown
  area it would go through the Permits and Licenses Committee and
  reviewed by planning and public works.
 Did the applicant come to the City for permits before they started
  working on their project or after they had started their project?
   Ms. Kay stated that as part of the Code Enforcement
  investigation, this case was referred to the Planning Division
  for entitlements.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Since it was mentioned that the applicant is conducting illegal
  dance parties and that this applicant has been doing illegal tenant
  improvement without permits, I am attempting to find out if both
  applicants are one in the same. It speaks to the character of the
  applicant if they are.
   Ms. Wilcox stated that the applicant would have to speak to that.

Chairman Springs asked if the applicant was on the AT&T phone line
and in attendance via teleconference.

Andrew Pociu, representative for TRIBE SF, is on the AT&T call line
and addressed the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 If he was the same applicant who conducted illegal dance parties
  upstairs as well as the applicant who is now doing illegal tenant
  improvements downstairs without permits, if they are one and the
  same?
   Mr. Pociu replied that they have only had one visit from Code
  Enforcement, and it was with regards to the previous Property
  Manager who allowed a children's party event to take place in
  the building upstairs, as they were personal friends of the
  Property Manager. That was back in February.
   Applicant also stated that they became owners of the property
  in July 2019 and anything before that date, they had nothing
  to do with.
 When was that particular party?
   Mr. Pociu stated that the party he was aware of was back in
  February 2019. It was a children’s party that was sanctioned
  by the previous property manager.
 Commissioner Rice stated that between July 2019 and January 2020,
  there were no parties or events or any illegal construction being
  done in the building that the applicant is aware of?
   Mr. Pociu stated that after the incident in February, that
  property manager is no longer working with them to insure that
  this type of action will no longer takes place.

**NOTE: Call was dropped** After 5 minutes, call reconnected through
AT&T Operator.

Commissioner Trejo stated she had questions for the applicant–
 The plan that is before the planning commission tonight is for a
  design review of the first floor coffee shop, correct?
   Mr. Pociu stated that is correct.
 Due to the report about the co-office spaces on both the second
  and third floors, if there are any uses that require permits you
  will be coming back to the City for those permits and reviews,
  correct?
   Mr. Pociu stated yes, they are now aware that they will need
  to have permits for any projects they attempt to undertake at
  their building.

Chairman Springs closed this segment and thanked the Planning
Commission for their input, and asked for a motion regarding Design
Review No. 2020-002 (DR-2020-002).

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Trejo to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-039 and adopt the attached resolution approving
DR-2020-002 Design Review DR-2020-002, subject to 8 conditions and
was seconded by Commissioner Patrick, that Resolution No. _1867_;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AN
  APPLICATION BY ANDREW POCIU, REPRESENTING TRIBE
  SF,INC.,  FOR  DESIGN  REVIEW  2020-002
  (DR-2020-002) TO ALLOW EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENTS TO
  A 700 SQUARE-FOOT TENANT SPACE WITHIN AN

  4

  EXISTING  THREE-STORY  16,350  SQUARE-FOOT
  MULTI-TENANT  COMMERCIAL  BUILDING  ON  AN
  APPROXIMATELY  7,000  SQUARE-FOOT  H-C
  (HISTORICAL CORE) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT 231
  SOUTH LA BREA AVENUE

Be approved.

Chairman Springs asked for questions and comments from the planning
commission.

Commissioner Trejo reiterated to the applicant the requirements for
obtaining permits prior to any work at this site?
  - Mr. Pociu stated that he was now aware and they will follow these
  requirements.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, and Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(7) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None. This was confirmed by the AT&T Operator, no one requested to
speak.

(8) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick stated -
1. Fireworks starting and its only June 3rd. Who does she contact
  to report these cases?
  - Mr. Jackson stated that Fireworks Public Service announcements
  will be going out throughout the City stating the designated
  time for fireworks here in Inglewood is only on July 4th, not
  after and not before. Anyone can always call Code Enforcement
  and leave a message with them, if you personally see someone
  who lights fireworks, that’s when you can call the Police
  Department.

Commissioner Rice stated –
1. That he wanted some follow up on the initiative he spoke about
  last month on Salon/Barber Colleges making money.
  - Mr. Jackson stated that Beauty Supply stores overview will be
  brought before the planning commission in the month of July,
  no excuses, and staff has been very busy with Zoom Meetings
  and being inundated with attempting to address those pressing
  issues. Staff looks to presenting at the next meeting.

Chairman Springs stated -
1. Property on 5th Avenue and 90th Street and the address is 9000 5th
  Avenue. The home is in a deplorable state and needs to be addressed,
  but by whom in the City?
  - Mr. Jackson stated that Code Enforcement will be out to look
  at the property and attempt to assist the resident.
2. Signage abuse on 5th Avenue and Manchester Blvd.
  - Mr. Jackson stated that the church was cited and served with
  the citation from Code Enforcement.
